samples.summary: Peer-supplied `lineAffinity` from Yorkie presence now drives local rendering with no runtime validation (type-only trust)
samples.evidence: Before this change the peer caret resolved a hardcoded `'backward'` (editor.ts:1588 old). Now `peer.position.lineAffinity` — a field that arrives verbatim over the wire from another collaborator's client presence (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:227` maps `p.presence.activeCursorPos` straight into `PeerCursor.position`, and :247 hands the same object to `editor.scrollToPosition`) — is fed into `resolvePositionPixel`. `DocsPresence.activeCursorPos.lineAffinity` (packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:29) is a compile-time union only; nothing validates the value at the deserialization boundary. Attack traced: a malicious/compromised collaborator publishes `activeCursorPos: { blockId, offset, lineAffinity: <arbitrary JSON> }`. I followed the value into `resolvePositionPixel` (peer-cursor.ts:111, :206) and `findPageForPosition` (pagination.ts:385-405); both only strict-compare against `'forward'`, so a hostile value degrades to the backward reading and no crash, unbounded loop, key lookup, or coercion path exists. Impact is therefore hardening only — the trust boundary widened without a validator, and the neighbouring untrusted fields (`blockId`, `offset`) are likewise unvalidated on this path. Worth a runtime narrow (`v === 'forward' ? 'forward' : 'backward'`) where peer presence is mapped in `buildPeerCursors`.
searchedFor: grep 'activeCursorPos|activeSelection' across the repo to enumerate every producer/consumer of peer presence
read packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:214-260 (buildPeerCursors, jumpToPeer) looking for a validator between presence and PeerCursor

samples.summary: Undo/redo caret restore now spreads the whole presence object instead of projecting `{blockId, offset}`, dropping an implicit field whitelist on data read back out of presence
samples.evidence: The undo (editor.ts ~2050) and redo (~2082) restores changed from `cursor.moveTo({ blockId: restoredPos.blockId, offset: ... })` to `cursor.moveTo({ ...restoredPos, offset: ... })`, and `restoreLocalCursor` likewise now spreads `...cursorPos`. `restoredPos` comes from `YorkieDocStore.getPresenceCursorPos()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2961-2979), which is an unchecked `as DocPosition` cast over a `Record<string, unknown>` presence blob. Any extra keys present on that object now land on `cursor.position` and are re-published verbatim by `recordHistoryPresence` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2950), which — unlike `updateCursorPos` → `clampPosToModel` (:957-972, which rebuilds a whitelisted `{blockId, offset, lineAffinity?}`) — publishes the caret object raw and unclamped. I could not complete an exploit chain: `getMyPresence()`/`getPresenceForTest(actorId)` return only this client's own presence, so the data is not peer-controlled, and object spread uses CreateDataProperty so an own `__proto__` key cannot pollute `Object.prototype`. Reported as a defence-in-depth regression (loss of the projection that previously sanitized presence-derived positions), not a confirmed vulnerability.
